marcadores.explicacao_original: Degenerating cartilage cells enlarge (hypertrophy), mature, and secrete alkaline phosphatase, which facilitates calcification of the matrix. A calcified matrix prohibits diffusion of nutrients, so chondrocytes die, leaving empty lacunae surrounded by a calcified cartilage matrix. These regressive stages occur in the aging process as well as in the epiphyseal plates of growing long bones.
